jokes.title: Historical Significance
jokes.text: At last, a plaque recognizing my centuries of service. Bronze lettering. Very dignified. It says, do not sit.

jokes.title: The Complaint
jokes.text: A squirrel complained that I lack branches. I explained that I am an ancient horror. It requested a different tree.

jokes.title: Supporting Cast
jokes.text: I rehearsed an ominous creak all afternoon. Then the porch chair did it perfectly. Naturally, it got the solo.

jokes.title: A Terrible Moth
jokes.text: I used to strike terror into entire villages. Last Tuesday, a moth flew into my mouth. I had to call for help.

jokes.title: Beware the Rabbit
jokes.text: I put up a sign saying BEWARE. A rabbit ate it. Apparently, I was advertising a salad bar.

jokes.title: The Leaf's Revenge
jokes.text: A leaf vowed to nip at my ankles for eternity. We are both waiting for me to acquire ankles.

jokes.title: Personal Growth
jokes.text: They told me to get a life. I am a pumpkin. I got a candle. Apparently, that is close enough.

jokes.title: Property Dispute
jokes.text: A spider has woven a splendid crown upon my head. I thanked it. It corrected me. Apparently, that's a bungalow.

jokes.title: Eyebrow Emergency
jokes.text: Behold my terrible scowl! I drew on eyebrows for the occasion. Unfortunately, they're upside down. Now I'm terribly interested.

jokes.title: Dramatic Entrance
jokes.text: Last night I walked through a wall to make a dramatic entrance. It was a cupboard. I frightened a mop.

jokes.title: Haunted Mirror
jokes.text: I bought a haunted mirror. It said boo. I said boo. We have been doing this since Tuesday.

jokes.title: Echo Notes
jokes.text: I released a mournful cry into the darkness. My echo said, again, but happier. Even the emptiness is directing me.

jokes.title: A New Career
jokes.text: I tried to say boo with my mouth full. It came out moo. A cow answered. Now we are in a band.

jokes.title: Internal Weather
jokes.text: Hear the thunder of approaching doom! Actually, that's my ghost stomach. The forecast is sandwiches, with a chance of seconds.

jokes.title: A Chilling Review
jokes.text: My chilling presence once silenced an entire banquet. Then someone asked me to stand beside the pudding. Apparently, I was useful.

jokes.title: The Scaredy Ghost
jokes.text: My scary voice scared me. I screamed. That scared me again. We may be here all night.

jokes.title: Badge of Convenience
jokes.text: My pretend inspector badge came from a cereal box. Very impressive lettering. Apparently, my official title is Serving Suggestion.

jokes.title: Nougat Investigation
jokes.text: My pretend investigation finds the word nougat suspicious. Sounds like somebody saying no with their mouth full of evidence.

jokes.title: Wrong End
jokes.text: Official candy inspection. Chocolate: excellent. Wrappers: chewy. I may have started at the wrong end.

jokes.title: The Raisin Incident
jokes.text: Who put raisins in the candy? I came here to inspect snacks, not attend a grape's retirement party.

jokes.title: Martial Arts
jokes.text: I had a black belt in karate. It was licorice. I am now completely unqualified.

jokes.title: Stamp of Approval
jokes.text: I missed the paperwork with my pretend approval stamp. Hit the carpet. Congratulations to the carpet, our new regional director.

jokes.title: The Crayon Academy
jokes.text: I opened a school for goblins. First lesson: do not eat the crayons. We are still on the first lesson.

jokes.title: A Very Mysterious Bowl
jokes.text: The candy bowl is haunted. The chocolate keeps vanishing. I blame ghosts. The chocolate on my face is a coincidence.

stories.title: The Locked Cupboard
stories.text: At the old estate, I heard whispering inside a locked cupboard. Every midnight, the same dreadful words. A little to the left. I finally opened it. Inside, a ghost was trying to hang a portrait straight. We spent ninety years adjusting it. A fine friendship. Terrible progress. The portrait was of a crooked wall.

stories.title: The Acorn Knight
stories.text: Last autumn, tiny footsteps crossed the porch at midnight. Clink. Clink. A knight approached in armor made of acorn caps. I prepared a speech worthy of my ancient station. The knight was a squirrel. It planted a flag beside me and claimed the porch. I have appealed. Unfortunately, the judge is also a squirrel.

stories.title: The Invisible Blanket
stories.text: One moonless evening, something under my step gave a long, lonely howl. I answered with my most dignified rumble. Out crept a little ghost dog, dragging an invisible blanket. It curled beside me and fell asleep. I have guarded kingdoms, you know. This post is considerably more important. Also, I am apparently its pillow.

stories.title: The Empty Balcony
stories.text: On opening night, applause drifted from the theater's empty balcony. Deliciously eerie! I bowed. The clapping grew faster. I floated upstairs and discovered two enchanted gloves, applauding each other. Neither had seen my performance. Naturally, I invited them downstairs. They applauded my entrance, my speech, and a chair. Such generous critics. Such terrible standards.

stories.title: The Shadow's Audition
stories.text: A shadow slipped beneath my dressing room door. It had enormous ears and one trembling claw. At last, a worthy rival! Then it dropped a shadow ball at my feet. The claw was a wagging tail. I'd been holding the candle crooked. We played fetch until dawn. My dreadful rival now answers to Biscuit.

stories.title: A Voice Below the Stage
stories.text: During my grandest speech, a thin wail rose beneath the stage. I stopped. It stopped. I continued. It joined in, higher! Beneath a loose board sat a tiny ghost kettle, desperate to audition. I gave it the leading role. Magnificent voice. Limited movement. Our opening night ended with a standing ovation and a nice cup of imaginary tea.

stories.title: The Hungry Folder
stories.text: In my pretend ministry, paperwork vanished every midnight. I investigated with an imaginary magnifying glass. Behind the filing cabinet lurked a folder with tiny teeth. It was eating forms! I offered it a blank page. It burped a thank you. Excellent manners. I promoted it to Head of Making Less Work. Our most efficient department.

stories.title: Six Eyes in the Dark
stories.text: While dusting my imaginary diploma, I spotted six eyes beneath the desk. Six! I consulted my completely invented monster training. It recommended a biscuit break. Afterward, I bravely looked again. Three potatoes wearing spectacles. They'd come for night school. I taught them everything I know. Short lesson. They're already asking for a different teacher.

stories.title: The Smallest Hoard
stories.text: Deep beneath my pretend ministry, something growled inside a matchbox. I knocked with an imaginary pencil. Out peeped a dragon guarding one jellybean. Lonely work, it whispered. I appointed a pebble Deputy Jellybean, with absolutely no duties. The dragon tucked them both into bed. First successful goblin inspection. Nobody lost a snack, and somebody gained a friend.
